newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ZLOTY STEADY VS BASKET, DEPOS SLIDE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ZLOTY STEADY VS BASKET, DEPOS SLIDE.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed unchanged against the basket of currencies on Monday, remaining pitted against resistance at three percent from parity, despite a brief morning slide mainly caused by importer orders.
"Importer orders coupled with some bank speculation pushed the zloty down in morning trade before position closing pulled the currency back up," said Marcin Stefaniuk, dealer at BDK SA.

Dealers said the zloty would likely remain just below the central bank's resistance barrier at three percent from parity for the next several days unless large client orders moved the local currency one way or another.
"The zloty may hold between 2.8 and 3.0 percent from parity if no large client flows change market sentiment," said Pawel Lopuszynski, forex dealer at Pekao SA.
The zloty closed at 2.96/2.93 percent from the trading band centre, flat from Friday's close at 2.98/2.90 percent after hitting intraday lows around 2.8 percent from parity.
Dealers said that a growing trade deficit, whiich last year doubled to about $12.6 billion not counting unregistered cross- border inflows, could weaken the zloty in the longer term.
"The widening trade deficit may, in the longer-term, curb the amount of currencies on the market," BDK's Stefaniuk said.

On the money market one-day rates slipped by one percentage point on Monday as banks, which already have suplusses on monthly reserve postions, braced for inflows from maturing NBP-bills and treasuries later this week, dealers said.
Overnight rates closed at 21.40/21.60 percent, down from opening's 22.40/22.59. Tomorrow/next were at 21.43/21.63 percent, down from opening's 22.45/22.61.
"One-day rates should fall below 21 percent in the near-term if the central bank again refrains from staging a drainage operation," said Wojciech Laciak, dealer at BPH SA.
